sanskrit: tam utpatantaṃ śayanād aśvatthāmā mahābalaḥ keśeṣv ālambya pāṇibhyāṃ niṣpipeṣa mahītale
english: As he sprang up from his couch, the mighty Aśvatthāman seized him by the hair with both hands and ground him down against the earth.

sanskrit: sa balāt tena niṣpiṣṭaḥ sādhvasena ca bhārata nidrayā caiva pāñcālyo nāśakac ceṣṭituṃ tadā
english: Crushed by him with main force, O Bhārata, and overcome by terror and by sleep, the prince of Pāñcāla could not so much as stir.

sanskrit: tam ākramya tadā rājan kaṇṭhe corasi cobhayoḥ nadantaṃ visphurantaṃ ca paśumāram amārayat
english: Pinning him down, O king, by the throat and by the chest with both his arms, he slew him as one slaughters a beast, while he roared and writhed.

sanskrit: tudan nakhais tu sa drauṇiṃ nātivyaktam udāharat ācāryaputra śastreṇa jahi mā mā ciraṃ kṛthāḥ tvatkṛte sukṛtāṃl lokān gaccheyaṃ dvipadāṃ vara
english: Clawing at the son of Droṇa with his nails, he spoke, scarcely able to make himself heard: "Son of the preceptor, slay me with a weapon, do not delay — let me, through you, O best of men, attain the worlds of the righteous."

sanskrit: tasyāvyaktāṃ tu tāṃ vācaṃ saṃśrutya drauṇir abravīt ācāryaghātināṃ lokā na santi kulapāṃsana tasmāc chastreṇa nidhanaṃ na tvam arhasi durmate
english: Hearing that faltering speech of his, the son of Droṇa replied: "There are no worlds for the slayers of preceptors, O disgrace of your line; therefore, vile one, you do not deserve death by a weapon."

sanskrit: evaṃ bruvāṇas taṃ vīraṃ siṃho mattam iva dvipam marmasv abhyavadhīt kruddhaḥ pādāṣṭhīlaiḥ sudāruṇaiḥ
english: So speaking, enraged, he battered that hero in his vital parts with his cruel heels and ankle-bones, as a lion mauls a rutting elephant.

sanskrit: tasya vīrasya śabdena māryamāṇasya veśmani abudhyanta mahārāja striyo ye cāsya rakṣiṇaḥ
english: At the cries of that hero being slain within the dwelling, O great king, the women and his guards awoke.

sanskrit: te dṛṣṭvā varṣmavantaṃ tam atimānuṣavikramam bhūtam eva vyavasyanto na sma pravyāharan bhayāt
english: Seeing him, towering and of more-than-human prowess, and taking him for some demon, they uttered not a word for fear.

sanskrit: taṃ tu tenābhyupāyena gamayitvā yamakṣayam adhyatiṣṭhat sa tejasvī rathaṃ prāpya sudarśanam
english: Having by that means dispatched him to the realm of Yama, the radiant one regained his fair chariot and mounted it.

sanskrit: sa tasya bhavanād rājan niṣkramyānādayan diśaḥ rathena śibiraṃ prāyāj jighāṃsur dviṣato balī
english: Issuing from that mansion, O king, and making the quarters resound, the mighty one drove on in his chariot through the camp, eager to slay his foes.

sanskrit: apakrānte tatas tasmin droṇaputre mahārathe saha tai rakṣibhiḥ sarvaiḥ praṇedur yoṣitas tadā
english: When that great warrior, the son of Droṇa, had departed, the women, together with all the guards, then broke into wailing.

sanskrit: rājānaṃ nihataṃ dṛṣṭvā bhṛśaṃ śokaparāyaṇāḥ vyākrośan kṣatriyāḥ sarve dhṛṣṭadyumnasya bhārata
english: Seeing their prince slain, all of Dhṛṣṭadyumna's warriors, plunged in bitter grief, cried out aloud, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: tāsāṃ tu tena śabdena samīpe kṣatriyarṣabhāḥ kṣipraṃ ca samanahyanta kim etad iti cābruvan
english: At their outcry the bulls among warriors close by quickly armed themselves and said, "What is this?"

sanskrit: striyas tu rājan vitrastā bhāradvājaṃ nirīkṣya tam abruvan dīnakaṇṭhena kṣipram ādravateti vai
english: But the terrified women, O king, catching sight of the son of Bharadvāja, cried out to them in piteous voices, "Make haste, give chase at once!"

sanskrit: rākṣaso vā manuṣyo vā nainaṃ jānīmahe vayam hatvā pāñcālarājaṃ yo ratham āruhya tiṣṭhati
english: "Whether demon or man we know not — he who, having slain the king of Pāñcāla, now stands mounted upon his chariot."

sanskrit: tatas te yodhamukhyās taṃ sahasā paryavārayan sa tān āpatataḥ sarvān rudrāstreṇa vyapothayat
english: Then those foremost of fighters at once surrounded him; but as they rushed upon him, he crushed them all with the weapon of Rudra.

sanskrit: dhṛṣṭadyumnaṃ ca hatvā sa tāṃś caivāsya padānugān apaśyac chayane suptam uttamaujasam antike
english: Having slain Dhṛṣṭadyumna and these his followers, he beheld Uttamaujas asleep upon his bed close by.

sanskrit: tam apy ākramya pādena kaṇṭhe corasi caujasā tathaiva mārayām āsa vinardantam ariṃdamam
english: Pinning him too with his foot, by the throat and the chest with main force, he slew that tamer of foes in the same way, even as he bellowed.

sanskrit: yudhāmanyus tu saṃprāpto mattvā taṃ rakṣasā hatam gadām udyamya vegena hṛdi drauṇim atāḍayat
english: But Yudhāmanyu came up, and thinking the man slain by a demon, raised his mace and swiftly struck the son of Droṇa upon the breast.

sanskrit: tam abhidrutya jagrāha kṣitau cainam apātayat visphurantaṃ ca paśuvat tathaivainam amārayat
english: Rushing upon him, he seized him and hurled him to the ground, and as he struggled like a beast, slew him in the very same way.

sanskrit: tathā sa vīro hatvā taṃ tato 'nyān samupādravat saṃsuptān eva rājendra tatra tatra mahārathān sphurato vepamānāṃś ca śamiteva paśūn makhe
english: Thus having slain that hero, the warrior fell next upon others — great chariot-fighters still asleep here and there, O lord of kings — while they writhed and trembled, as a slaughterer dispatches the beasts at a sacrifice.

sanskrit: tato nistriṃśam ādāya jaghānānyān pṛthagjanān bhāgaśo vicaran mārgān asiyuddhaviśāradaḥ
english: Then, taking up his sword, skilled in swordsmanship, he ranged the paths division by division and cut down others, the common folk.

sanskrit: tathaiva gulme saṃprekṣya śayānān madhyagaulmikān śrāntān nyastāyudhān sarvān kṣaṇenaiva vyapothayat
english: And spying out in the picket the sentries lying within it, weary and with their weapons laid aside, he crushed them all in a single moment.

sanskrit: yodhān aśvān dvipāṃś caiva prācchinat sa varāsinā rudhirokṣitasarvāṅgaḥ kālasṛṣṭa ivāntakaḥ
english: Fighters, horses, and elephants he hewed down with his excellent sword, all his limbs drenched in blood, like Death let loose by Time.

sanskrit: visphuradbhiś ca tair drauṇir nistriṃśasyodyamena ca ākṣepeṇa tathaivāses tridhā raktokṣito 'bhavat
english: By those who writhed beneath him, by the wielding of his sword, and by its very swinging, the son of Droṇa was drenched in blood in three ways at once.

sanskrit: tasya lohitasiktasya dīptakhaḍgasya yudhyataḥ amānuṣa ivākāro babhau paramabhīṣaṇaḥ
english: As he fought, soaked in blood, his blazing sword in hand, his form shone more-than-human, utterly terrible to behold.

sanskrit: ye tv ajāgrata kauravya te 'pi śabdena mohitāḥ nirīkṣyamāṇā anyonyaṃ drauṇiṃ dṛṣṭvā pravivyathuḥ
english: And those who lay awake, O Kaurava, bewildered too by the din, gazing upon one another, beheld the son of Droṇa and quailed.

sanskrit: tad rūpaṃ tasya te dṛṣṭvā kṣatriyāḥ śatrukarśanāḥ rākṣasaṃ manyamānās taṃ nayanāni nyamīlayan
english: Beholding that form of his, the warriors, harriers of foes, took him for a demon and shut their very eyes.

sanskrit: sa ghorarūpo vyacarat kālavac chibire tataḥ apaśyad draupadīputrān avaśiṣṭāṃś ca somakān
english: Terrible of form, he ranged the camp then like Death, and caught sight of the sons of Draupadī and the surviving Somakas.

sanskrit: tena śabdena vitrastā dhanurhastā mahārathāḥ dhṛṣṭadyumnaṃ hataṃ śrutvā draupadeyā viśāṃ pate avākirañ śaravrātair bhāradvājam abhītavat
english: Alarmed by that din, those great car-warriors, the sons of Draupadī, bows in hand — having heard that Dhṛṣṭadyumna was slain, O lord of peoples — covered the son of Bharadvāja with showers of arrows, undaunted.

sanskrit: tatas tena ninādena saṃprabuddhāḥ prabhadrakāḥ śilīmukhaiḥ śikhaṇḍī ca droṇaputraṃ samārdayan
english: Then, roused by that uproar, the Prabhadrakas and Śikhaṇḍin assailed the son of Droṇa with their shafts.

sanskrit: bhāradvājas tu tān dṛṣṭvā śaravarṣāṇi varṣataḥ nanāda balavan nādaṃ jighāṃsus tān sudurjayān
english: But the son of Bharadvāja, seeing them pouring down their rains of arrows, gave a mighty roar, eager to slay those near-invincible foes.

sanskrit: tataḥ paramasaṃkruddhaḥ pitur vadham anusmaran avaruhya rathopasthāt tvaramāṇo 'bhidudruve
english: Then, beside himself with wrath and recalling his father's slaughter, he leapt down from the floor of his chariot and rushed upon them in haste.

sanskrit: sahasracandraṃ vipulaṃ gṛhītvā carma saṃyuge khaḍgaṃ ca vipulaṃ divyaṃ jātarūpapariṣkṛtam draupadeyān abhidrutya khaḍgena vyacarad balī
english: Taking up in battle a broad shield blazoned with a thousand moons and a great celestial sword adorned with gold, the mighty one charged the sons of Draupadī and ranged among them with his blade.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa naraśārdūlaḥ prativindhyaṃ tam āhave kukṣideśe 'vadhīd rājan sa hato nyapatad bhuvi
english: Then that tiger among men struck Prativindhya in the belly in that fray, O king, and he, slain, fell to the earth.

sanskrit: prāsena viddhvā drauṇiṃ tu sutasomaḥ pratāpavān punaś cāsiṃ samudyamya droṇaputram upādravat
english: Having pierced the son of Droṇa with a lance, the valiant Sutasoma raised his sword again and rushed upon Droṇa's son.

sanskrit: sutasomasya sāsiṃ tu bāhuṃ chittvā nararṣabhaḥ punar abhyahanat pārśve sa bhinnahṛdayo 'patat
english: But that bull among men severed Sutasoma's sword-bearing arm and struck him again in the side; his heart cloven, he fell.

sanskrit: nākulis tu śatānīko rathacakreṇa vīryavān dorbhyām utkṣipya vegena vakṣasy enam atāḍayat
english: Then the valiant Śatānīka, son of Nakula, heaving up a chariot-wheel with both arms, struck him swiftly upon the chest.

sanskrit: atāḍayac chatānīkaṃ muktacakraṃ dvijas tu saḥ sa vihvalo yayau bhūmiṃ tato 'syāpāharac chiraḥ
english: But the brāhmaṇa struck Śatānīka, who had let fly the wheel; reeling, he sank to the ground, and then he struck off his head.

sanskrit: śrutakarmā tu parighaṃ gṛhītvā samatāḍayat abhidrutya tato drauṇiṃ savye sa phalake bhṛśam
english: Then Śrutakarman, seizing an iron club and rushing in, struck the son of Droṇa hard upon his left buckler.

sanskrit: sa tu taṃ śrutakarmāṇam āsye jaghne varāsinā sa hato nyapatad bhūmau vimūḍho vikṛtānanaḥ
english: But he smote that Śrutakarman upon the face with his excellent sword; slain, he fell to the ground, senseless, his countenance disfigured.

sanskrit: tena śabdena vīras tu śrutakīrtir mahādhanuḥ aśvatthāmānam āsādya śaravarṣair avākirat
english: At that din the hero Śrutakīrti, the great archer, closed with Aśvatthāman and covered him with showers of arrows.

sanskrit: tasyāpi śaravarṣāṇi carmaṇā prativārya saḥ sakuṇḍalaṃ śiraḥ kāyād bhrājamānam apāharat
english: Warding off his rains of arrows too upon his shield, he struck from the trunk his shining head with its earrings.

sanskrit: tato bhīṣmanihantā taṃ saha sarvaiḥ prabhadrakaiḥ ahanat sarvato vīraṃ nānāpraharaṇair balī śilīmukhena cāpy enaṃ bhruvor madhye samārdayat
english: Then the slayer of Bhīṣma, together with all the Prabhadrakas, the mighty one, smote that hero on every side with weapons of every kind, and struck him too with a shaft between the brows.

sanskrit: sa tu krodhasamāviṣṭo droṇaputro mahābalaḥ śikhaṇḍinaṃ samāsādya dvidhā ciccheda so 'sinā
english: But the mighty son of Droṇa, possessed by wrath, closed with Śikhaṇḍin and clove him in two with his sword.

sanskrit: śikhaṇḍinaṃ tato hatvā krodhāviṣṭaḥ paraṃtapaḥ prabhadrakagaṇān sarvān abhidudrāva vegavān yac ca śiṣṭaṃ virāṭasya balaṃ tac ca samādravat
english: Having slain Śikhaṇḍin, that scorcher of foes, filled with wrath, swiftly fell upon all the bands of the Prabhadrakas, and charged too what remained of Virāṭa's host.

sanskrit: drupadasya ca putrāṇāṃ pautrāṇāṃ suhṛdām api cakāra kadanaṃ ghoraṃ dṛṣṭvā dṛṣṭvā mahābalaḥ
english: And among the sons of Drupada, his grandsons, and his friends, the mighty one wrought dreadful carnage, striking each down as he sighted them.

sanskrit: anyān anyāṃś ca puruṣān abhisṛtyābhisṛtya ca nyakṛntad asinā drauṇir asimārgaviśāradaḥ
english: Closing upon men one after another, the son of Droṇa, skilled in the sword's arts, hewed them down with his blade.

sanskrit: kālīṃ raktāsyanayanāṃ raktamālyānulepanām raktāmbaradharām ekāṃ pāśahastāṃ śikhaṇḍinīm
english: A dark woman, red of mouth and eye, garlanded and anointed in red, robed in red, standing alone, noose in hand, her hair in a single braid —

sanskrit: dadṛśuḥ kālarātriṃ te smayamānām avasthitām narāśvakuñjarān pāśair baddhvā ghoraiḥ pratasthuṣīm harantīṃ vividhān pretān pāśabaddhān vimūrdhajān
english: they beheld her, the Night of Doom, standing there with a smile, binding men, horses, and elephants with her dreadful nooses and setting forth, dragging off sundry spirits, noose-bound and shorn of their hair.

sanskrit: svapne suptān nayantīṃ tāṃ rātriṣv anyāsu māriṣa dadṛśur yodhamukhyās te ghnantaṃ drauṇiṃ ca nityadā
english: Her, leading off the sleepers in their dreams, those foremost of fighters had seen on other nights too, O honored one, and the son of Droṇa ever slaying.

sanskrit: yataḥ pravṛttaḥ saṃgrāmaḥ kurupāṇḍavasenayoḥ tataḥ prabhṛti tāṃ kṛtyām apaśyan drauṇim eva ca
english: From the time the battle of the Kuru and Pāṇḍava hosts began, from then onward they had been seeing that fell apparition and the son of Droṇa as well.

sanskrit: tāṃs tu daivahatān pūrvaṃ paścād drauṇir nyapātayat trāsayan sarvabhūtāni vinadan bhairavān ravān
english: Those already struck down by fate beforehand, the son of Droṇa afterward laid low, terrifying all beings, roaring his fearful roars.

sanskrit: tad anusmṛtya te vīrā darśanaṃ paurvakālikam idaṃ tad ity amanyanta daivenopanipīḍitāḥ
english: Recalling that vision of former days, those heroes, pressed hard by fate, thought, "This is the very thing."

sanskrit: tatas tena ninādena pratyabudhyanta dhanvinaḥ śibire pāṇḍaveyānāṃ śataśo 'tha sahasraśaḥ
english: Then at that uproar the archers in the camp of the Pāṇḍavas awoke, by hundreds and by thousands.

sanskrit: so 'cchinat kasya cit pādau jaghanaṃ caiva kasya cit kāṃś cid bibheda pārśveṣu kālasṛṣṭa ivāntakaḥ
english: Of one he cut off the feet, of another the loins; some he clove through the sides, like Death let loose by Time.

sanskrit: atyugrapratipiṣṭaiś ca nadadbhiś ca bhṛśāturaiḥ gajāśvamathitaiś cānyair mahī kīrṇābhavat prabho
english: With men savagely mangled, with others crying out in extremity of pain, and with still others crushed by elephants and horses, the earth was strewn, O lord.

sanskrit: krośatāṃ kim idaṃ ko 'yaṃ kiṃ śabdaḥ kiṃ nu kiṃ kṛtam evaṃ teṣāṃ tadā drauṇir antakaḥ samapadyata
english: "What is this? Who is this? What is that noise? What — what has been done?" — as they cried thus, the son of Droṇa became their very Death.

sanskrit: apetaśastrasaṃnāhān saṃrabdhān pāṇḍusṛñjayān prāhiṇon mṛtyulokāya drauṇiḥ praharatāṃ varaḥ
english: The Pāṇḍavas and Sṛñjayas, stripped of weapons and armor yet frantic, the son of Droṇa, the best of smiters, sent forth to the world of the dead.

sanskrit: tatas tacchastravitrastā utpatanto bhayāturāḥ nidrāndhā naṣṭasaṃjñāś ca tatra tatra nililyire
english: Then, terrified by his blade and starting up in panic, blind with sleep and bereft of their wits, they cowered here and there.

sanskrit: ūrustambhagṛhītāś ca kaśmalābhihataujasaḥ vinadanto bhṛśaṃ trastāḥ saṃnyapeṣan parasparam
english: Their thighs grown stiff, their strength struck down by faintness, crying out, sorely affrighted, they trampled one another underfoot.

sanskrit: tato rathaṃ punar drauṇir āsthito bhīmanisvanam dhanuṣpāṇiḥ śarair anyān preṣayad vai yamakṣayam
english: Then the son of Droṇa mounted again his fearfully-rumbling chariot, and bow in hand, with his arrows sent yet others to the realm of Yama.

sanskrit: punar utpatataḥ kāṃś cid dūrād api narottamān śūrān saṃpatataś cānyān kālarātryai nyavedayat
english: Some of those noblest of men who started up again, even from afar, and other brave ones who rushed in, he made over to the Night of Doom.

sanskrit: tathaiva syandanāgreṇa pramathan sa vidhāvati śaravarṣaiś ca vividhair avarṣac chātravāṃs tataḥ
english: And so, crushing them with the front of his chariot, he raced about, and rained down upon his enemies showers of arrows of every kind.

sanskrit: punaś ca suvicitreṇa śatacandreṇa carmaṇā tena cākāśavarṇena tadācarata so 'sinā
english: And again, with his richly-wrought hundred-mooned shield, sky-hued, and with that sword, he plied his work.

sanskrit: tathā sa śibiraṃ teṣāṃ drauṇir āhavadurmadaḥ vyakṣobhayata rājendra mahāhradam iva dvipaḥ
english: Thus the son of Droṇa, frenzied for battle, churned up their camp, O lord of kings, as an elephant churns a great lake.

sanskrit: utpetus tena śabdena yodhā rājan vicetasaḥ nidrārtāś ca bhayārtāś ca vyadhāvanta tatas tataḥ
english: At that din the fighters started up, O king, out of their senses, sick with sleep and stricken with fear, and ran this way and that.

sanskrit: visvaraṃ cukruśuś cānye bahvabaddhaṃ tathāvadan na ca sma pratipadyante śastrāṇi vasanāni ca
english: Others screamed out in discordant voices and spoke much that was incoherent, and they could not find their weapons or their garments.

sanskrit: vimuktakeśāś cāpy anye nābhyajānan parasparam utpatantaḥ pare bhītāḥ ke cit tatra tathābhraman purīṣam asṛjan ke cit ke cin mūtraṃ prasusruvuḥ
english: Others, their hair come loose, did not recognize one another; some, springing up in terror, wandered there in confusion; some voided their bowels, and some let flow their urine.

sanskrit: bandhanāni ca rājendra saṃchidya turagā dvipāḥ samaṃ paryapataṃś cānye kurvanto mahad ākulam
english: And, O lord of kings, snapping their tethers, horses and elephants and others careered about together, working a great tumult.

sanskrit: tatra ke cin narā bhītā vyalīyanta mahītale tathaiva tān nipatitān apiṃṣan gajavājinaḥ
english: There some men, in fear, flung themselves flat upon the earth, and the elephants and horses crushed them as they lay fallen.

sanskrit: tasmiṃs tathā vartamāne rakṣāṃsi puruṣarṣabha tṛptāni vyanadann uccair mudā bharatasattama
english: While all this was going on, O bull among men, the demons, glutted, roared aloud in their glee, O best of the Bharatas.

sanskrit: sa śabdaḥ prerito rājan bhūtasaṃghair mudā yutaiḥ apūrayad diśaḥ sarvā divaṃ cāpi mahāsvanaḥ
english: That sound, O king, raised by the hosts of spirits in their joy, filled all the quarters and the very heavens, a mighty roar.

sanskrit: teṣām ārtasvaraṃ śrutvā vitrastā gajavājinaḥ muktāḥ paryapatan rājan mṛdnantaḥ śibire janam
english: Hearing their cries of anguish, the elephants and horses, terror-struck and broken loose, careered about, O king, trampling the people in the camp.

sanskrit: tais tatra paridhāvadbhiś caraṇodīritaṃ rajaḥ akaroc chibire teṣāṃ rajanyāṃ dviguṇaṃ tamaḥ
english: The dust raised by their hooves as they raced about made the darkness in their camp twofold in the night.

sanskrit: tasmiṃs tamasi saṃjāte pramūḍhāḥ sarvato janāḥ nājānan pitaraḥ putrān bhrātṝn bhrātara eva ca
english: When that darkness had fallen, the people were bewildered on every side: fathers knew not their sons, nor brothers their brothers.

sanskrit: gajā gajān atikramya nirmanuṣyā hayā hayān atāḍayaṃs tathābhañjaṃs tathāmṛdnaṃś ca bhārata
english: Riderless elephants ran down elephants and horses ran down horses, striking, shattering, and trampling, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: te bhagnāḥ prapatantaś ca nighnantaś ca parasparam nyapātayanta ca parān pātayitvā tathāpiṣan
english: Broken and falling and striking one another, they brought others down, and having felled them, trampled them flat.

sanskrit: vicetasaḥ sanidrāś ca tamasā cāvṛtā narāḥ jaghnuḥ svān eva tatrātha kālenābhipracoditāḥ
english: Out of their senses, heavy with sleep, and wrapped in darkness, the men there slew their own, driven on by Time.

sanskrit: tyaktvā dvārāṇi ca dvāḥsthās tathā gulmāṃś ca gaulmikāḥ prādravanta yathāśakti kāṃdiśīkā vicetasaḥ
english: Abandoning the gates, the gatekeepers, and the sentries their pickets, fled with all their might, witless and seeking any way out.
